title: cost-opt: autotune defaults for batching/caching + quant profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Ava Chen
release_notes: Add automatic/default recommendation engine for batching and KV-prefix caching; introduce pre-defined quantization profiles and a unit-economics CLI to simulate cost impact for common workloads.
description:
Motivation: customers want predictable per-token unit economics with sensible defaults that reduce cost without manual tuning. This PR introduces an autotune pipeline that recommends and applies defaults for batching, prefix/KV caching and model quantization profiles, plus a small unit-economics CLI to simulate expected cost/latency tradeoffs for a given route/model workload distribution.

What this change does: 1) Adds a new autosuggest service (internal API) that computes recommended default batching window, max batch size, and cache TTLs based on observed request distributions and model latency profiles. 2) Adds three safe quantization profiles (safe-8bit, balanced-4bit, aggressive-4bit+) with metadata describing expected throughput/quality deltas for common architectures. 3) Integrates recommendations into the router so newly created routes can opt into "autotune defaults" flag; existing routes are not mutated automatically. 4) Ships a unit-economics CLI tool (tools/unit_econ/simulate) that accepts a small workload histogram and returns estimated tokens/sec, cost-per-1M-tokens, and 95th-percentile latency under different config permutations. 5) Adds telemetry events and dashboards entries so operator and product can measure realized savings and quality regressions.

Implementation notes: - Autosuggest service implemented in services/autotune (Go) with a lightweight local simulation engine reusing existing runtime kernels. - Batching and cache defaults propagate via runtime config: runtime/batching/config_defaults.go and runtime/cache/defaults.go. - Quantization profiles live in models/quant_profiles.json and are consumed by the model registry onboarding flow. - Unit econ tool is a small Python CLI with a reproducible sim harness (tools/unit_econ). - Safety: profiles marked with expected quality delta and rollback guardrails in case of eval score regressions. - Backwards compatible: routes must explicitly enable "autotune_defaults": true to opt-in.

Testing & validation: - Unit tests for autosuggest heuristics and CLI (go test, pytest). - E2E smoke tests in perf-canary that run representative prompts against a canary pool with and without recommendations. - Local evaluation harness measured median latency improvements 12-18% and cost reductions 8-20% across three representative workloads; aggressive profile showed larger savings but ~1.5-2.5% quality delta on a small eval set.

Checklist: - [x] Autosuggest service implementation and unit tests - [x] Runtime defaults wiring (batch/cache) - [x] Quant profiles and registry integration - [x] Unit-econ CLI & docs - [x] Telemetry metrics + dashboard PR linked - [x] Perf canary runs green

Notes for reviewers: focus review on the autosuggest heuristics (services/autotune/heuristics.go) and the conservative default values in runtime/batching/config_defaults.go. I included a small simulation log (tools/unit_econ/example_runs/summary.md) in the diff for context.
commits: 93100a: initial autosuggest service and basic heuristic implementation
93100b: expose autotune_defaults flag in route API + migrate router logic
review_comments: Samir Patel: Nice end-to-end. A few questions on heuristics.go: why do we pick 50ms as base window for short-tail workloads? Can we parameterize this?
Ava Chen (author): Good point - made base window configurable with an env var and added note to docs. Default remains 50ms for now based on perf-canary data.

Linnea Berg: Please add a unit test covering scenario where caching TTLs cause measurable P95 regression due to cold-start misses. Also add guardrail that prevents applying aggressive profile to routes with <5k requests/day.
Ava Chen (author): Added test and implemented min-traffic check in autosuggest service. See services/autotune/heuristics_test.go and added validation in service.go.
Diego Martinez: telemetry looks good. Can we tag events with model.family and route.tags to make dashboarding easier?
Ava Chen (author): Done - events include model_family and route_tags labels now. Added dashboard query examples to docs.
